title: A CycleMin descent onto the cheap band [n, 19n] cannot start a=2
statement: After a descending even run from a peak at least n^2 onto an odd p in [n, 19n], the next odd-run length a(p) cannot be 2. Hence cheap OOE starts exist only in the initial climb from the cycle minimum, so N_cheap is O(1) rather than o-e, and L=25781 dies at floor 10^6.
counterexamples: One-even descent: p=1000057 lies in [1000001, 19000019], a(p)=2, and the even-cell peak 1000057^2 is at least n^2

Post-OOE descent: 1000057 --OOE--> peak 31626832356906 --E--> 5623773; the landing is in the cheap band and a(5623773)=2. In the window [10^6+1, 10^6+20001) there are 297 such a=2 landings out of 1210 cheap-band OOE landings
The named 6187 descent 11189→1087→189 is not a CycleMin witness and is not a cheap-band a=2 return
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / descent next-run type
notes: Phase 0 only. Not a reopen of valley-coupling return-cost or ordered pairs. No Lean, no Paper A edit, no leftover-killer from this census. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: n=10^6+1; cheap band [n, 19n]; OOE starts on [n, n+20000); 6187 Q-path 11189→1087→189
